name: manual_5c30e6
claim: An append-only event log (GossipBus-style: emit() is a plain INSERT, state is derived by folding events) cannot provide compare-and-swap on its own -- a read-validate-then-emit sequence (like a claim-board's claim operation) has a real TOCTOU race between separate OS processes, no matter how tight the code looks. The fix is a small side table with a UNIQUE/PRIMARY KEY constraint on the contested key (e.g. task_id), used ONLY as the exclusion point (INSERT, catch IntegrityError) -- keep the existing business-logic validation (status checks, dependency checks) as-is, the side table just closes the gap after them. Remember to release the row on every path that makes the resource reclaimable again (retry/requeue), not just on final completion, or a legitimate future claim gets permanently blocked by its own stale exclusion row.

decisions.notes: Fixed a real TOCTOU race in PT's scripts/agent_coordination.py _queue_claim (2026-07-12), found during a code review of the GossipBus claim board this session had been live-using all day. The previous 'concurrent' test only awaited two claims sequentially and never exercised the actual race window; a new asyncio.gather()-based test proved the fix and caught that the retry path also needed the release call, which the first draft of the fix missed.
